sc: Fever in a malaria area, positive RDT, no danger signs → Oral artemether–lumefantrine
Positive film, coma or convulsions, Hb < 5 g/dL → Severe malaria: IV artesunate
Child treated for malaria, dark urine a few days later → Blackwater fever (haemolysis)
f: Fever, chills, sweats, headache, vomiting · severe: prostration, convulsions, breathing difficulty, dark urine
Pallor, splenomegaly, jaundice · severe: coma, acidotic breathing, shock, bleeding
Thick and thin film = gold standard · RDT (HRP2 stays positive, cannot follow response) · Hb · glucose
Impaired consciousness, prostration, convulsions · Hb < 5 g/dL · glucose < 2.2 mmol/L · acidosis · shock · jaundice · parasitaemia > 10%
Uncomplicated: artemether–lumefantrine 3 days · severe: IV artesunate 3 mg/kg (< 20 kg) at 0, 12, 24 h then daily · rectal 10 mg/kg before referral
Cerebral malaria · severe anaemia (transfuse) · hypoglycaemia · acidosis · AKI · blackwater fever
trap: Treat malaria only after a positive test · comatose child: check glucose first · vivax/ovale relapse: primaquine (check G6PD) · sickle cell trait protects; sickle cell disease does not
